We need P(defective | X+, Y-). Use Bayes.

Let D be defective, ND not defective.

Prior P(D)=1/3, P(ND)=2/3.

Likelihoods:

P(X+|D)=3/4, P(Y+|D)=2/3, so P(Y-|D)=1-2/3=1/3. Since tests independent conditional on D, P(X+ & Y-|D) = (3/4)*(1/3)=3/12=1/4.

Similarly for ND: P(X+|ND)=1/4, P(Y+|ND)=1/3, so P(Y-|ND)=2/3. Then P(X+ & Y-|ND)= (1/4)*(2/3)=2/12=1/6.

Now posterior:

P(D | data) = P(D)*L_D / [P(D)*L_D + P(ND)*L_ND] = (1/3)*(1/4) / [ (1/3)*(1/4) + (2/3)*(1/6) ].

Compute numerator: 1/12.

Denominator: 1/12 + (2/3)*(1/6) = 1/12 + (2/18) = 1/12 + 1/9 = common denominator 36: 3/36 + 4/36 =7/36.

Thus posterior = (1/12) / (7/36) = (1/12)*(36/7)=3/7.

Thus answer A.

Return A only.
